dimensions.explanation: The operative text addresses licensed corporations and the listed non-centrally cleared equity options. It does not expressly state whether every licensed corporation counterparty, transaction capacity, or geographic booking location is included.

The circular defines the collective term “non-centrally cleared equity options” by listing single-stock options, equity basket options and equity index options. It does not define “licensed corporation” beyond the Code reference.

The exemption is stated for the listed instruments, but no additional conditions (such as reporting, monitoring, counterparty class or trade purpose) are stated in the SFC operative text. EU monitoring/reporting is described as foreign background and could be mistakenly treated as an SFC condition.
“Will exempt” announces an SFC decision, while the Code paragraph “will be amended accordingly and gazetted in due course” leaves the legal mechanism and interim force unresolved.

The announced period begins 4 January 2026 and lasts “until further notice”; the amendment is to be gazetted later, so the relationship between announcement date, commencement date and gazettal is unresolved.

Applicability depends on instrument classification, absence of central clearing, licensed-corporation status, the Part III Schedule 10 requirement, and whether the circular operates before gazettal. EU and UK materials explain alignment but do not themselves determine SFC scope.

questions: Does the announced exemption have operative effect from 4 January 2026 before the Part III Schedule 10 amendment is gazetted?
Does “licensed corporations” cover all transactions of a licensed corporation, including offshore booking or counterparties outside the SFC perimeter?
Are any EU-style monitoring or reporting conditions intended to apply in Hong Kong, or are they explanatory background only?
What precise contractual or product features determine that an option is a single-stock, equity-basket or equity-index option and is non-centrally cleared?

assumptions: The selected control concerns whether an SFC licensed corporation may treat a specified option exposure as exempt from the SFC margin requirement on a stated date.
The option is classified as one of the three listed types and is not centrally cleared.
No EU or UK condition is imported unless the SFC text expressly adopts it.

citations.quote: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) issues this circular to inform licensed corporations that it will exempt non-centrally cleared single-stock options, equity basket options and equity index options (collectively, “non-centrally cleared equity options”) from its margin requirements1 from 4 January 2026 until further notice to align with the latest global developments.
As set out in Part III of Schedule 10 to the Code of Conduct for Persons Licensed by or Registered with the Securities and Futures Commission (Code of Conduct).

readings.distinction: Reading A treats the circular as an operative announcement: from 2026-01-04, the listed non-centrally cleared equity options are exempt for licensed corporations, despite the later gazettal statement. The foreign EU and UK provisions are alignment context only.

assumptions: The Code amendment and gazettal are prerequisites for operative legal exemption.
The announcement signals intended future alignment but does not itself disapply the existing Part III requirement before gazettal.

citations.quote: Paragraph 7(e) of Part III of Schedule 10 to the Code of Conduct will be amended accordingly and gazetted in due course.
The margin requirements for non-centrally cleared equity options were originally scheduled to take effect on that date.

The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) issues this circular to inform licensed corporations that it will exempt non-centrally cleared single-stock options, equity basket options and equity index options (collectively, “non-centrally cleared equity options”) from its margin requirements1 from 4 January 2026 until further notice to align with the latest global developments.

readings.distinction: Reading B treats the circular as a prospective policy announcement whose operative effect depends on the promised Code amendment and gazettal. Before that event, the existing margin requirement remains applicable; after gazettal, the listed options are exempt from 2026-01-04 or the gazettal commencement date, whichever the amendment specifies.
questions: The text does not state whether gazettal is constitutive, merely formal, or retroactive to 2026-01-04.
The text does not specify the commencement date in the eventual amendment.
readings.statement: [TRUE_IS_SATISFIED] Under the gazettal-dependent reading, the exemption condition is satisfied only once the required Code amendment has been gazetted and its commencement requirements are met; the circular alone does not establish that condition before then.
